caption: Figure 1.1. The evidence-to-defence architecture: eight inquiry routes, four controls and nine gates.
short_title: The evidence-to-defence architecture: eight inquiry routes, four controls and nine gates
alt_text: A three-row serpentine architecture. Eight inquiry routes enter a nine-gate chain: Project Start Pack, Problem, Evidence, Design, Execution, Claim, Argument, Editorial and Defence Readiness. SCOPE, CORPUS and DECIDE are local controls at the Problem, Evidence and Design gates. TRACE spans the chain. A dashed return path shows that new evidence may reopen an earlier gate.

caption: Figure 1.2. Advice, approval, authority and assistance do not transfer authorship or responsibility.
short_title: Advice, approval, authority and assistance do not transfer authorship or responsibility
alt_text: A central student box owns authorship, execution, verification, decision records and defence. Arrows enter from the supervisor for advice and academic approval, institutional authority for rules and assessment, an external organisation for context and access and an AI tool for candidate assistance. None transfers responsibility for the submitted record.

The decision must be continue, narrow, pivot or stop. A dashed feedback path returns narrowed or pivoted work to SCOPE; only supported continuation reaches the gate.

caption: Figure 3.2. The CORPUS cycle and its retained evidence records.
short_title: The CORPUS cycle and its retained evidence records
drawing_title: CORPUS cycle with retained evidence records

Collect produces a Search Strategy Record; Organise produces a Source Ledger and identity map; Read produces a Core Source Note; Probe produces an Appraisal Record; Use produces a Claim–Evidence Map; Synthesise produces a Synthesis Memo and Corpus Statement. Arrows show the iterative cycle and dashed links connect each retained record to the central pack.

caption: Figure 6.2. The claim stress-test and gate return paths.

caption: Figure 7.1. Gate records, answer architecture and manuscript section functions.
short_title: Gate records, answer architecture and manuscript section functions
drawing_title: Gate records, answer architecture and manuscript section functions
alt_text: Three horizontal layers distinguish authorised gate records, a seven-step answer architecture and manuscript section functions. Problem, Evidence, Design, Execution and Claim records feed a central spine running from question through position, route, evidence, result and boundary to contribution. The lower layer shows introduction, knowledge position, method or design, results or findings and discussion or conclusion. A note states that records are sources rather than pre-written chapters and that every reuse must preserve identity and boundary.

caption: Figure 7.2. Section contract and paragraph reasoning test.
short_title: Section contract and paragraph reasoning test
drawing_title: Section contract and paragraph reasoning test
alt_text: A five-step section contract runs from promise through evidence set, reasoning and boundary to return. A separate four-step paragraph test runs from claim through evidence and reasoning to a limit or hand-off. Two notes state that a section earns its place only when the next step depends on what it establishes and that a citation or result beside a claim is insufficient without a visible reasoning link and boundary.

caption: Figure 8.1. Semantic-first revision and proof-control pipeline.
alt_text: A semantic-first editorial pipeline moves from the accepted study through macro, meso and micro revision, package control and Microsoft Word proof. Semantic drift in evidence, comparison, uncertainty, population, causal status or claim scope returns to the earliest responsible gate. Technical defects trigger a cycle of DOCX repair, all-story field update, tagged PDF export, every-page inspection and proof recording. The final status distinguishes author-side closed with proof pending from author-side proof verified with administrative and publisher checks still pending.

caption: Figure 8.2. One-study consistency across headline, authorship and manuscript layers.
short_title: One-study consistency across headline, authorship and manuscript layers
alt_text: An authoritative study containing the question, executed route, evidence, principal result and boundary supplies title, verified author identity, keywords, abstract, introduction, results, discussion, limitations, conclusion and version metadata. An equivalence test requires every interface to describe the same study and bounded answer. Compression may omit detail but may not change identity, count, uncertainty or claim scope; detected drift is repaired at the earliest layer where it entered.

caption: Figure 9.1. From author-side closure to a defence-ready institutional record.
short_title: From author-side closure to a defence-ready institutional record
drawing_title: Author-side closure to defence-ready institutional record
alt_text: A five-stage chain moves from author-side closure through a current authority map, an assessable institutional record and controlled performance interfaces to defence readiness. One bounded contribution must preserve one title, route, evidence body, claim boundary and assistance record. Scientific identity drift, inaccurate declarations, unsafe evidence or unresolved authority conflicts require a return to the earliest responsible control. Final checks confirm current rules, identified files, accurate declarations, lawful evidence and tested recovery.
